news.title: French prosecutor wants ex-Asian football chief Bin Hammam tried over 2022 Qatar World Cup vote
news.lede: The move is part of a probe launched in 2019 which is focusing on the role Bin Hammam played on the eve of the vote that awarded the competition to Qatar. PARIS – France’s financial prosecutor’s office has asked that four people, including disgraced former Asian football chief Mohamed Bin Hammam, be sent to trial for corruption in connection with the awarding of the 2022 World Cup to Qatar. The move at the end of August, confirmed to AFP, comes three years after a magistrate in Paris issued an international arrest warrant for Bin Hammam, who has been banned for life from football following accusations of corruption and conflicts of interest. It is part of a probe launched in 2019 which is focusing on the role played by Bin Hammam in the actions of Reynald Temarii, ex-president of the Oceania Football Confederation (OFC), on the eve of the vote that awarded the competition to Qatar.

news.title: World Cup coach reappointed two months after stepping down
news.lede: Ghana have reappointed Carlos Queiroz as manager just two months after he stepped down in the wake of their World Cup campaign. Queiroz, 73, was only named head coach of the Black Stars two months out from the tournament finals, succeeding Otto Addo who was sacked following emphatic defeats by Austria and Germany. The former Manchester United assistant manager guided Ghana through the group stage, which included a goalless draw with England, before they were knocked out by Colombia in the round of 32. Amid a down period in Ghana’s footballing history, having enduring the humiliation of not qualifying for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, a knockouts finish in the World Cup was hardly a failure for Queiroz.

Lionel Messi has officially retired from international football, and a little-known FIFA regulation means Argentina will be forced to hand his famous number 10 shirt to a new player rather than hang it up permanently. Messi announced on August 31, two days after Argentina lost to Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final. While many observers had already sensed the final would be his last cap, the formal confirmation still came as a jolt to the football world.

news.title: Singapore to host Brazil, Japan, Paraguay in star-studded football festival
news.lede: Singapore will host a series of blockbuster football fixtures during the Fifa international window in November, including a World Cup rematch between Brazil and Japan, organisers announced on Thursday. The Mizuho Blue Challenge will also involve the hosts and Paraguay, with four matches taking place in the space of five days at the city’s National Stadium at The Kallang. Singapore will take on Paraguay in the opening fixture on November 13, with Japan and Brazil facing off a day later in a rematch of their last 32 clash in Houston, which the South Americans won 2-1. A double-header on November 17, with Singapore taking on the five-time World Cup winners and Japan battling Paraguay, promises to be the highlight of the week at the 55,000-seat venue.

news.title: National Stadium to stage football friendlies involving Brazil, Japan, Paraguay and Singapore
news.lede: Brazil's Vinicius Jr (in yellow) in action against Japan's Ao Tanaka during their World Cup clash on June 29. Brazil won the match 2-1. SINGAPORE – The World Cup may have ended in July, but football fans here will get to experience world-class sporting action again when the National Stadium at The Kallang hosts Brazil, Japan and Paraguay, as well as the Lions in November. The Mizuho Blue Challenge – The Kallang Football Series Singapore will see four matches played between Nov 13 and 17, organisers The Kallang Group and Dentsu Sports International announced on Sept 3.
